The minimum detectable difference of a paired, clustered design

Source: R/core-bench-ni.R
hr_mdd.Rd

hr_mdd() gives the smallest paired accuracy difference a benchmark of n_items items can detect, and hr_n_needed() the number of items needed to detect a given one. Both use the closed form for a paired comparison of two proportions with a true difference of 0:

Usage

hr_mdd(
  n_items,
  n_clusters = NULL,
  m = NULL,
  icc = NULL,
  p_disc = NULL,
  cv = 0,
  power = 0.8,
  alpha = 0.025,
  n_contrasts = 1,
  holm = TRUE
)

hr_n_needed(
  delta,
  m = NULL,
  icc = NULL,
  p_disc = NULL,
  cv = 0,
  power = 0.8,
  alpha = 0.025,
  n_contrasts = 1,
  holm = TRUE,
  true_diff = 0
)

# S3 method for class 'hr_mdd'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'hr_n_needed'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

n_items

The number of scored items.

n_clusters

The number of clusters the items fall in, or NULL. With m left NULL, m = n_items / n_clusters.

m

The mean number of items per cluster, or NULL. With both m and n_clusters left NULL the items are taken as independent (m = 1).

icc

ICC_D, the intra-cluster correlation of the paired item difference, in [0, 1). Required when m > 1; take it from a pilot on the dev split.

p_disc

The share of items on which the two arms disagree, in (0, 1]. Required.

cv

The coefficient of variation of cluster sizes, 0 for equal clusters.

power

The power, in (0, 1).

alpha

The one-sided significance level, in (0, 0.5). 0.025 matches a one-sided 97.5% bound.

n_contrasts

The number of confirmatory contrasts in the Holm family.

holm

Whether to adjust alpha for Holm over n_contrasts.

delta

The difference to detect, as a proportion (0.08 for 8 points).

true_diff

The true difference assumed for a non-inferiority test, at most 0: the test must then tell -delta from true_diff, so the gap is delta + true_diff.

x

An hr_mdd or hr_n_needed.

...

Ignored.

Value

hr_mdd() returns an object of class hr_mdd, a list with mdd and the design it rests on: n_items, n_clusters, m, m_adj (the size after the cv correction), icc, cv, de, n_eff, p_disc, power, alpha, alpha_adj, n_contrasts, holm, df (C - 1), the t quantiles t_alpha and t_power the MDD uses, and the normal quantiles z_alpha and z_power beside them. hr_n_needed() returns an object of class hr_n_needed with n_eff, n_items (n_eff x DE) and n_clusters (n_items / m, NA when m is not given), unrounded, beside the same design values, df (n_items / m - 1) and the quantiles. print() rounds them up: with m given it rounds the clusters up first and prints that many clusters of m as the items, so n_items 837.8 at m = 6 prints as 840 items in 140 clusters.

Details

n_eff = (t_(C - 1, 1 - alpha') + t_(C - 1, power))^2 x p_disc / Delta^2,

with t quantiles on C - 1 degrees of freedom for C clusters: the degrees of freedom of the cluster-robust t bound that hr_report() tests non-inferiority with. p_disc is the share of items on which the two arms disagree, so p_disc / n_eff is the variance of the mean paired difference. Items in one cluster are not independent, so the effective number of items is n_eff = n_items / DE with the design effect DE = 1 + (m - 1) x ICC_D (Kish 1965), where m is the mean cluster size and ICC_D the intra-cluster correlation of the paired item difference, not of raw accuracy. With unequal cluster sizes of coefficient of variation cv, m is replaced by (cv^2 + 1) x m (Eldridge, Ashby and Kerry 2006). hr_mdd() solves for Delta:

Delta = (t_(C - 1, 1 - alpha') + t_(C - 1, power)) x sqrt(p_disc / n_eff).

C is n_clusters, or n_items / m when only m is given, or n_items when the items are independent; it must be above 1. hr_n_needed() finds the number of items whose C = n_items / m satisfies the formula, by root finding, since the quantiles depend on it.

With holm = TRUE and more than one contrast, alpha' = alpha / n_contrasts, the level Holm's procedure tests its first contrast at: the worst case, since later steps test at larger levels. With holm = FALSE, alpha' = alpha.

The closed form is a first estimate. Power for a study is better planned by simulation from a pilot fitted on the dev split. Set against the report's cluster-robust t bound (dev/sim-power.R, 2000 replicates, seed 1), the MDD at 80% power was 0.16 and 0.17 points below the simulated one at 80 equal clusters (one and nine contrasts; simulated power at the formula's MDD 78.55% and 78.30%) and 0.25 points above it at 40 unequal clusters (81.60%). Normal quantiles in place of the t quantiles were 0.26 and 0.41 points below at 80 clusters (77.20% and 76.05%) and 0.04 points below at 40 (79.85%).

References

Eldridge, S. M., Ashby, D. and Kerry, S. (2006). Sample size for cluster randomized trials: effect of coefficient of variation of cluster size and analysis method. International Journal of Epidemiology 35(5), 1292-1300.

Kish, L. (1965). Survey Sampling. Wiley.

See also

hr_register_contrasts(), hr_report()

Other harness: gr_arm(), gr_qa_reference(), gr_scorer_answer(), hr_arm(), hr_benchmark(), hr_contrast(), hr_drift_check(), hr_reference(), hr_report(), hr_scorer()

Examples

# 480 scored questions in 80 documents, ICC of the paired difference 0.2,
# the arms disagreeing on 20% of items.
hr_mdd(480, n_clusters = 80, icc = 0.2, p_disc = 0.2)
#> <hr_mdd> 8.2 points at 80% power, one-sided alpha 0.025
#>   480 items in 80 clusters (m = 6, 6 after cv 0), ICC_D 0.2: DE 2, n_eff 240
#>   p_disc 0.2

# The same design after Holm over nine confirmatory contrasts.
hr_mdd(480, n_clusters = 80, icc = 0.2, p_disc = 0.2, n_contrasts = 9)
#> <hr_mdd> 10.7 points at 80% power, one-sided alpha 0.002778 (0.025 / 9 contrasts, Holm worst case)
#>   480 items in 80 clusters (m = 6, 6 after cv 0), ICC_D 0.2: DE 2, n_eff 240
#>   p_disc 0.2

# Items and documents needed for an 8-point margin under that Holm family.
hr_n_needed(0.08, m = 6, icc = 0.2, p_disc = 0.2, n_contrasts = 9)
#> <hr_n_needed> 8.0 points at 80% power, one-sided alpha 0.002778 (0.025 / 9 contrasts, Holm worst case)
#>   n_eff 419 effective items; DE 2, so 840 items in 140 clusters of 6
